subject: Post-call: throughput & latency runbook + proposed GPU sizing
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Park <joe.park@acme.energy>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@acme.energy>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: throughput targets, streaming needs, and next steps

Joe / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of requirements (from call)
- Peak concurrent sessions: 120 concurrent users for the pilot (expected to 250 in 6 months)
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 200ms for short-completion assistant (prompt+response tokens ~ 50-150)
- Streaming: real-time streaming is required for the UI; prefix tokens and session cache expected
- Throughput: sustained 150 requests/minute during business hours (bursty up to 600 rpm for short windows)
- Model candidate: open-weights Llama-3-70B / quantized variant for cost targets
- Data residency: US-only (VPC/private deployment later)

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Redwood to share a short runbook with sizing options (GPU types, reserved throughput, expected qps per instance) — action: Sean, by EOD tomorrow.
2) Acme to share a representative prompt set (50 prompts) and token distribution — action: Joe, by EOD Thu.
3) Proof-of-concept booking (2-week dedicated pool) — initial quote + scope to follow.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf (initial sizing options) and gpu-comparison-table.csv (throughput estimates by GPU).

If anything above is incorrect, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll circulate a concrete sizing recommendation and a short perf validation plan.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Joe Park <joe.park@acme.energy>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@acme.energy>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput targets, streaming needs, and next steps

Thanks Sean — that aligns with what we heard on the call. Couple clarifications: 
- The 120 concurrent users are interactive agents that each keep a KV cache (average session length ~2m). Some sessions will stream continuously for longer.
- For the latency SLO, we care about end-to-end UI latency (browser-to-server streaming start + token throughput). If you include network overhead we want to remain < 250ms 95p.
- For the PoC we can fund the two-week dedicated pool but will need a rough cap on TCO before greenlighting.

I’ll upload the prompt set by Thursday. Can your sizing doc show expected p95/99 latency for each GPU option (A100, H100, and the cheaper 80GB A800-class alternatives)? Also useful: expected cost per 1M tokens for the pilot.

– Joe
Director of Product | Acme Energy
joe.park@acme.energy

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput targets, streaming needs, and next steps

Looping in sizing recommendations and perf validation notes — I did a first-pass read of Sean's attachments. Notes: 

- Baseline assumptions to call out in the runbook: tokenization variance (avg tokens/request), kv-cache hit rate assumptions, and batching strategy. Those change qps->latency mapping a lot.
- For streaming requirements we should recommend a dual-path: low-latency single-token streaming for interactive sessions (dedicated low-batch workers) + background high-throughput workers for long-form completions.
- Suggest explicitly showing two reserved pool sizes: Pilot (2x H100 equiv nodes) and Scale (4x H100 equiv). Also include the A100 and 80GB A800 alternatives with notes on quantization tradeoffs.

I’ve attached a quick GPU comparison table (gpu-comparison-table.csv) with measured tokens/sec and 95p latencies from our test harness for the Llama-3-70B quantized path. Use these as the source for the PoC quote.

Marissa
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Park <joe.park@acme.energy>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@acme.energy>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed sizing + perf validation plan for Acme pilot

Joe / Priya — attached is a short, pragmatic plan and a recommended sizing ladder. High level:

Sizing ladder (pilot -> scale):
- Option A (lower cost, conservative perf): 3 x A800-80GB nodes (quantized FP4) — expected sustained 120 concurrent sessions, p95 ~ 220-280ms, burst headroom ~2.5x
- Option B (balanced): 2 x H100-80GB nodes (mixed-precision) — expected sustained 150 concurrent sessions, p95 ~ 140-200ms, better streaming startup latency
- Option C (performance-first): 2 x H100 + 2 x A100 (mixed pool) — sustained 300 concurrent sessions, p95 < 160ms under recommended batching strategy

Notes on assumptions:
- Token distribution input from Acme is required to finalize exact sizes. KVs assumed avg hit rate 68%.
- We include prefix caching and per-session KV allocation to reduce overall compute when sessions are hot.
- The p95 numbers include internal network hops (pod->model host) but not customer-edge WAN; add ~20-30ms network tail for remote offices.

Perf validation plan (2-week PoC)
Week 1: model onboarding + baseline tests
- Onboard Llama-3-70B quantized artifact
- Run our perf harness with Acme prompt set (95/99 latency sweeps, streaming start latency)
Week 2: scaled soak & SLO verification
- Soak at 150 sustained users for 24h, burst tests to 600 rpm
- Run regression checks against quality metrics (per prompt set)

Cost estimate (ballpark for 2-week PoC)
- Option A: $12k
- Option B: $18k
- Option C: $30k

Deliverables
- PoC dot-matrix report with p95/p99 numbers, token costs, and runbook for production sizing.
- If Acme signs PoC funding, we’ll reserve the dedicated pool and schedule a kickoff.

I can run the perf harness against a seed of Acme prompts as soon as you upload them. Sean — I’ll need the formal signal to move the PoC quote to finance.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Priya Raman <priya.raman@acme.energy>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sizing + perf validation plan for Acme pilot

Thanks all — this is very helpful and clear. We reviewed the options internally and lean toward Option B (2 x H100) for the PoC to hit the latency targets without overcommitting. A couple of asks before we finalize: 
1) Can you include a very short appendix showing expected p95/p99 under a lower KV hit rate scenario (35-40%)? We have some user segments that will be cold.
2) Please provide a capped TCO for the two-week PoC (we have a max contribution of $20k).

If you can get the appendix + final quote into DocuSign by EOD Monday we’ll pull the budget and sign.

Joe and I will upload the prompt set today.

– Priya
Sr. Eng Manager | Acme Energy
priya.raman@acme.energy
